JUDGEMENT CALLS (both are plain 4-way crossings - the only two on the sheet - and both were read as junctions):
* S14 (520,469): the middle column (R#3 above, R#7 below) meets the middle horizontal. inkmap shows the vertical unbroken from y=447 to y=491 and the horizontal unbroken from x=498 to x=542, with no semicircular hop, no sideways jog, and no blob fatter than the union of two ~3 px strokes. Read as JUNCTION. As a crossing it would give {R#3 bottom, R#7 top} as an isolated 2-terminal series link and {C#5 right, V#2 bottom, R#6 top} separately - electrically legal, so this rests on the ink prior (this dataset's drafters draw a hop when they mean 'not connected') plus the obvious intent of a ladder network whose rungs meet at nodes.
* S25 (532,596): the middle column (R#7 above, GND stem below) meets the bottom rail. Same pixel picture - vertical unbroken y=572..620, horizontal unbroken, no jog (the hop score of 2.1 is a false positive from the slight rightward drift of the column). Read as JUNCTION. The crossing reading would leave the ground node holding only {R#7 bottom, GND}, i.e. a ground reference that is not the return path for either source or for the 10mA current source - the whole bottom rail would float. That is the decisive argument here.
* The other three CRITICAL sites are unambiguous Ts and were recorded as junctions after inspecting their crops: S6 (514,335) the top rail with the 4k column dropping off it; S12 (738,458) the middle horizontal landing on the right rail; S15 (297,476) the middle horizontal branching off the left rail.
